audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings tell the reader to defend with Null Sphere's shield - spikes[0] 'Q-shield the moment the trap lands', early "spend Q's shield to absorb the burst of his trade", whys[1] 'Your Q shield absorbs a hook trade', whys[3] 'your shield blanks his dismounted trades', whys[5] 'your Q shield plus blink farm through his poke', spikes[2] 'your Q shield plus Nether Blade mana sustain'. The shield absorbs MAGIC damage and Kled is physical throughout. The page half-notices this in mid - "Your passive's 15% magic reduction does nothing against an AD champion here" - and then in the very next clause says 'it is your Q shield and your blink that carry the lane', exempting a tool that fails for exactly the same reason.
audit.why: The reader banks a cooldown as armour six separate times and it absorbs nothing. What the page should be saying instead is the mechanic that actually governs the matchup and is missing from both layers: Skaarl TAKES THE DAMAGE FOR KLED. Your burst does not kill a mounted Kled, it dismounts him - and a dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions and has to fight to rebuild Courage before he can remount. That reframes the whole assassination plan: you are not looking for a one-shot, you are looking to strip the mount and then win the version of him that is left. Second omission: Jousting can be RECAST to dash back through the target, so he has two dashes, not one.
audit.corrected: The magic shield re-tasked to what it can actually do here; Skaarl's damage-soak and the reduced champion damage while dismounted written into early, mid and the interactions block; Jousting's recast added.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (P: 'Skaarl, who takes damage for him. When Skaarl's health depletes, Kled dismounts. While dismounted... he deals less damage to champions'; E: 'Kled can cast this ability again to dash back through his initial target')

audit.whatIsWrong: Beartrap on a Rope is named matchup-defining in six places - 'count it out loud if you must' - and no cooldown appears anywhere in either layer. Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is named twice with no cooldown and no range.
audit.why: Beartrap is 11/10/9/8/7s, which is what 'count it out loud' is supposed to mean. Violent Tendencies is 13/12/11/10/9s and is an auto-attack reset, so the four-attack burst is telegraphed by the wind-up rather than by an ability cast. Jousting is 13/12/11/10/9s and recastable. Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110s at 3500/4000/4500 range - effectively a map-wide engage, which is a very different threat from the lane tool the page implies. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: Beartrap's 11s, Violent Tendencies' 13s reset, Jousting's 13s recast and the ultimate's 140s at 3500+ range written into the spikes, mid and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Kled six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while whys[2] says 'you trade evenly', whys[3] says 'you climb back toward even', whys[4] calls Level 6 'your spike', whys[5] says 'you own the tempo', and mid opens 'This is where the lane flips to you'. Only whys[6] agrees with the chart, and it is the one stage that genuinely belongs to Kled.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 66.67%, though on only 6 games. The sample is too thin to lead with, but five of the seven whys already describe a lane that has turned, and the chart records none of it - this is an internal-consistency fix more than a data-driven one.
audit.corrected: Level 3 and Levels 4-5 set to Skill, Level 6 and First item flipped to Kassadin, in both layers. 2+ items left with Kled, where whys[6] and late both agree he out-scales in a brawl.
sources: content whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], whys[5], mid

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says 'Null Sphere can interrupt' with no object - interrupt what? And nothing describes how the hook actually resolves, though it is the ability the page tells you to fear most.
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels; nothing in Kled's kit is a channel, so the claim is empty and a reader may hold their Q waiting to interrupt something that will never happen. The genuinely useful mechanic instead: Beartrap deals its bonus physical damage and yanks you toward Kled only IF THE SHACKLE HOLDS FOR A SHORT DURATION - the pull is not instantaneous, so a landed trap is a moment to react in rather than a done deal.
audit.corrected: The empty interrupt claim removed and replaced with the shackle's delay before the yank.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (Q: 'If shackled for a short duration, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled')

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the part you simply have to survive — mounted Kled is a hard early bully and you are at your most helpless, with only Null Sphere and no dash. His Beartrap on a Rope (Q) hooks you in, and Violent Tendencies turns the follow-up autos into a free all-in, so never step into hook range to last-hit. Eat the minion-deny, spend Q's shield to absorb the burst of his trade, and take CS at max range. Do not try to trade back before Nether Blade is online — your mana will not sustain it and you lose every level 1-3 skirmish into his Courage bar.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the part you simply have to survive - mounted Kled is a hard early bully and you are at your most helpless, with only Null Sphere and no dash. Beartrap on a Rope (Q) hooks you on an 11-second cooldown, and Violent Tendencies resets his auto for a four-hit burst, so the weapon wind-up is the tell. Never step into hook range to last-hit. Your Q shield absorbs magic and every point of his damage is physical, so spend it on last-hits instead of saving it as armour, and take CS at max range until Nether Blade is online.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to you. Once Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore is online and Q is maxed you can farm under tower and weather his dismounted Pocket Pistol poke, and at 6 Riftwalk changes everything — blink over his Jousting dash, blink out of the Skaarl remount window, and dodge the Beartrap hook that used to kill you. Bait the mounted Q, then once it is on cooldown blink in for a Force Pulse cone and back out before he can remount. Your passive's 15% magic reduction does nothing against an AD champion here — it is your Q shield and your blink that carry the lane, so stop being free pressure and start farming even.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Once Nether Blade's quintupled mana restore is online and Q is maxed you can farm under tower, and at 6 Riftwalk changes everything - blink over his Jousting dash, which he can recast to come straight back through you, and dodge the hook that used to kill you. Understand what you are fighting: Skaarl takes the damage for Kled, so your burst does not kill a mounted Kled, it dismounts him - and dismounted he deals less to champions and must earn Courage back before remounting. Void Stone and the Q shield are both magic-only against a physical kit, so HP and the blink carry you. Bait the mounted Q, then blink in for a Force Pulse cone and out.

edits.before: Your goal is to be the one assassinating his carries before a remounted Skaarl matters. With Rod of Ages online and Riftwalk ramping, your blink-spam lets you ignore his frontline and delete his backline — that is the game you played the whole early for. But be honest: Kled is the harder scaler in a drawn-out brawl, and once he remounts with full Courage at 2+ items his sustained mounted DPS and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! engage out-trade your single-target burst. Use your mobility to pick and end before he gets a full build, and never duel a mounted Skaarl head-on.
edits.after: Your goal is to be the one assassinating his carries before a remounted Skaarl matters. With Rod of Ages online and Riftwalk at 2s, your blink-spam lets you ignore his frontline and delete his backline - that is the game you played the whole early for. Use your mobility to pick and end before he gets a full build, and never duel a mounted Skaarl head-on.
